_about: The Magic Portals port's rolling stones and barrel blasts: what a stone breaks, when it
counts as touching, and what a blast breaks. See docs/planning/2026-09-11-magic-portals-

_note: Entity names a rolling stone breaks whether or not the placement sets
metadata/breakable. The Godot project breaks only what the flag marks (hazards.gd:117-120).
Eight breakable_wall placements carry no flag: levels 8, 12, 18, 21 (two), 23 and 24
of chapter 1, and level3a. That is the original's own scene data, not the converter:
each is an inline entity in its .esc whose CustomData lacks breakable, and Ethanon
reads an inline entity as it stands (ETHEntityProperties.cpp:202-224). So the
original decides by something the data does not show. The owner played it, and on
11 September confirmed that stones broke those walls.
DECODED since (planning step 115): the stone's side is ETHBeginContactCallback_breakable_wall
(MiscCallbacks, listing L68341), which Ethanon binds by the ENTITY's name (ETHASUtil.cpp:63-67)
and which never reads 'breakable': #1-14 tests the other body's 'demolisher', #16-33 its
speed against scale(1.5), #35-40 destroy(thisEntity). So every breakable_wall, flagged or
not, breaks for a stone - the owner's testimony, from the bytecode. The flag is read only
by isBreakable (L67923), which is a blast's grab (the blast block below).
breakable._source: owner testimony, 11 September 2026; ETHBeginContactCallback_breakable_wall (listing L68341) #1-40, planning step 115

_note: What a rolling stone does to the PLAYER it begins to touch (planning step 160, STK). ETHBeginContactCallback_rolling_stone
(listing L68515, MiscCallbacks bytes 346486..347456) #107-129: where isCharacter(other) - the player is the only
entity with that datum (GameCharacter::GameCharacter L22977, built by one class, MainCharacter) - and the stone's
hitIntensity is above 2.5 (CMPIf against 0x40200000, JNP skips, so STRICTLY above), other.SetInt('hp', 0): the same
write a death area makes (L66942 #9-18), so the death is a death area's - blood, the player hidden, the lost screen,
no sound of its own (GameStateController::checkGameLost L23649 #3-63). hitIntensity is #6-56:
dp2(the STONE's own GetLinearVelocity, normalize(other.GetPositionXY() - thisEntity.GetPositionXY())) / getScale()
- the stone's speed toward the player's entity point, over 50 px a unit (D11_check C47: 2.5 is 125 level units a
second of the original's physics). A stone at rest (#34-35: length 0 skips the whole callback) or moving away kills
nothing, and the player's own movement is not in the number. A begin-contact only. The stone is untouched. Carried by
rolling_stone.ent in both spellings, placed, launched or dropped by the beholder - not rolling_stone_no_emissive.ent
(2-30), which has no callback of its own. The beholder's rocks are the same callback, and the port kills with them in
Boss::Contacts (boss.json rock.crush_intensity, the same 2.5), which this does not replace.
The number the port tests is the impact watch's, the one the stone's own shake reads (Impacts::Begin::Approaching):
the fastest the stone came along that line since it last met or left something. INFERRED equal to the callback's, not
measured: no footage shows a stone against the player (docs/parity-backlog.md STK-1).
stone._source: ETHBeginContactCallback_rolling_stone L68515 #6-56 (hitIntensity), #107-129 (the kill, 2.5); isCharacter L66695; GameCharacter::GameCharacter L22977; ETHBeginContactCallback_death_area L66942; checkGameLost L23649 (out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt, md5 48fe65ce)

_note: How near a stone must come to a breakable's box to touch it. The Godot project's stone
breaks what it touches (body_entered), and a solver leaves a body resting against a
wall touching it rather than overlapping it, so the port's overlap test grows the
box by this much. A threshold of the port's, not a measurement.
What a barrel bomb's blast breaks. explode (MiscCallbacks, listing L67590) grabs with an
EntityGrabber of radius scale(80) filtered by isBreakableOrExplosiveOrBurnable (#33-47;
fire.json blast.radius_px), keeps each entity whose first contact on the line from the
blast is itself (#63-109, getFirstContactExcept with NonProjectileChooser), and sets its
'destroy' to 1 (#111-122). isBreakable (L67923) is GetUInt('breakable') != 0: the FLAG,
never the name, so the eight flagless breakable_walls above are not grabbed as
breakables. ETHCallback_breakable_wall (L68771) #1-86 reads isDestroyed and deletes the
wall with its wall_destroy and startEarthquake(20 x destroyEffectScale), the same frame:
the barrel's callback is a dynamic entity's, the wall's a static one's, and
ETHScene::Update runs the static entities' callbacks after the dynamic ones'
(ETHScene.cpp:464-491). Footage F6 (2-12) shows the wall gone in the frame
explosion_large first shows (#160).
entities: the breakables whose own callback is ETHCallback_breakable_wall, in either
spelling (callbacks bind by RemoveExtension of the name, 00_order 8.0 rule 4).
blast._source: explode L67590 #33-47, #111-122; isBreakable L67923; ETHCallback_breakable_wall L68771 #1-86 (out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt)
